title: Alpha index: published/alpha/<date>.json (served at /alpha/<date>.json), written by `wire alpha-index <date>`. One file per day with every Alpha signal, built from the stance labels. No post text, no claim text.

date.description: the Pacific day the index is for: the day's podcast run and X scan

generated_at.description: ISO 8601 with Pacific offset; the file is rebuilt by later runs

complete.description: false when a source was missing or not fully labelled when this was built; `missing` says which. Never wait on it: read what is here and read again later.

id.description: stable: the same stance label always has the same id

date.description: the day the claim or post was made, Pacific

target.description: what the signal is about, in words: the company, or the sector or market

stance.description: -2 clearly bearish .. 2 clearly bullish; 0 (a mention) is not a signal and is left out

role.description: the speaker's role, or `X account, <type>`, or `unknown`

link.description: podcast: the video or episode link at the moment (&t=<seconds>); X: the post

posted_at.description: X: when the post was made, ISO 8601 Pacific

source_id.description: the episode id, or the X post id

origin.description: primary: first-hand (an operator on their own business, a data source, someone giving their own view). recap: relaying news or someone else's view.

horizon_days.description: trading days the call is judged over

inferred.description: fields filled by Wire's default rule because the reader gave none

target.description: what the ticker is, in words

label.description: the 5-step scale on `net`, or Mixed when meaningful weight sits on both sides (see wire/alpha_sentiment.py: the lighter side weighs at least 0.5 and is at least 25% of both sides)

net.description: weighted mean of the speakers' votes on the stance scale; one vote per speaker (mean of their posts), primary weight 1, recap 0.5

speakers.description: distinct speakers with a bullish or bearish vote

neutral.description: speakers who mentioned it with no call (or whose own posts cancel out); they carry no weight in `net`

primary_share.description: share of the voting speakers that are first-hand (origin primary)

agreement.description: |bull weight - bear weight| / (bull weight + bear weight): 1 when every voter is on one side

dispersion.description: weighted standard deviation of the votes around `net`, in stance units

confidence.description: high: 3 or more voting speakers, half or more primary; low: one speaker or no primary voter; else medium

rank.description: speakers x |net|; for a Mixed ticker speakers x dispersion. The order of this list, best first

reason.description: what was said, in Wire words and never the counts: one or two distinct claims, or ▲ bullish claim · ▼ bearish claim when both sides spoke

tickers.description: The day's X signals added up per US-listed ticker (X only: podcast signals are not in it), best rank first. A day file built before this field existed has none.

markets.description: The same for the market targets @MARKET, @RATES and @CREDIT (rates read bullish when easing is expected).
